initiative.title: Bring tsx-data-flow into srcly
initiative.summary: srcly is the fast big-picture base layer; tsx-data-flow becomes a background TS/TSX data-flow engine whose evidence lands in srcly's metrics, findings, code viewer, reports, compare, and later the dependency view.
initiative.next_action: Pro threads refine mapping branches; then plan the first proof: move engine into engine/, export contract, one metric + markers.

sources.anchor: product priority order; code map primary surface
Views table; Explore it in the browser
Findings row; Metrics end-to-end; Code viewer; Graph views

claims.statement: srcly is the home and base layer; tsx-data-flow features merge into it.
srcly's speed must be preserved; data flow never delays the base render.
Value order: reports, problem spotting linked to code, improved code view, then dep view augmented with full data flow.
Analysis correctness (compiler-backed identity, strict tsconfig) outranks everything else in tsx-data-flow.
Markdown output exists for agent handoff: dense, grounded, concise next action.
tsx-data-flow's own overview/report pages are transitional and need not survive.
Several Pro threads will detail branches and update this map.
Single repository: engine moves into srcly (workspace/monorepo layout only if needed).
tsx-dataflow-serve UI goes away; focus on best versions of features in srcly.
Distribution delegated to agent: choose most robust. Chosen: esbuild bundle in the wheel, system node>=18, project typescript with bundled fallback, N/A without node.

themes: data-flow graph as the end state

conflicts.statement: tsx-data-flow says the code map is its primary surface; srcly's primary surface is the map/treemap with a modal code viewer.
conflicts.resolution: srcly's treemap stays primary; the code viewer absorbs code-map overlays (path on source, markers, where-used).

shape.appetite: Program delivered as independently revertible slices, one srcly home per slice.
shape.problem: Two tools with overlapping shells; srcly is fast but tree-sitter-only, tsx-data-flow is deep but slow and has its own UI.
shape.recommended_shape: Integrate at the data level: tsx-data-flow runs as a findings-style background Node job emitting one versioned srcly export; srcly maps it into catalog metrics, findings, markers, report artifacts, compare, and later dependency-view edges.

feature_mapping.srcly_home: findings/ (new dataflow tool) + catalog metrics + markers

feature_mapping.tsx_feature: Per-file burden, path depth, representation changes, defensive ops

feature_mapping.srcly_home: catalog metrics with witnesses; later dependency-view edges

Overview page, file rows, report tab strip, tsx-dataflow-serve
feature_mapping.srcly_home: none (covered by explorer/Hot Spots); tsx-dataflow-serve retired, not migrated

success_moves: Reuse the findings runner pattern (timed job, process-group kill, fingerprint cache, overlay) instead of a new job system.
Define one versioned export contract first and test its join against srcly paths/lines before any UI.
Express every numeric signal as a catalog metric so picker, Hot Spots, treemap, compare, and report derive automatically.
Keep the layer optional: N/A with reasons, base scan unaffected when Node/tsconfig is missing.
Defer dependency-view data flow until graph legibility and tsx trajectory UI stabilize.
Prove on examples/bad-ish-solid and srcly's own client before larger repos.

first_proof.question: Can the engine's output join srcly's tree and code viewer cleanly without slowing the base layer?
first_proof.artifact: One catalog metric (impossible defenses) + its finding markers from a dataflow job on examples/bad-ish-solid and srcly client/.
first_proof.decision_rule: Proceed to the full metric set and reports if paths/lines join exactly, counts match markers, and the layer lands within ~10s on client/; otherwise fix the export contract first.

rabbit_holes: Embedding tsx-data-flow's SPA or route-totality graph wholesale.
200K-LOC repos: engine takes ~120s; needs scoping (changed files, per-package) or a skip rule.
Monorepos with many tsconfigs: bound projects like MAX_TSC_PROJECTS.
Wheel size from bundled TypeScript fallback; measure in first proof.

history.event: Initiative created; intent and shape drafted from the user's request plus both repos' docs.
Resolved D1 (single repo, engine/ package), D2 (bundle in wheel, delegated), D3 (retire serve UI). Shape updated; no downstream artifacts invalidated.
